label: OPENING WEEK FILE
openingMemo: The upstairs fax now follows Graham Mercer’s Private Line through the full NFL week. Graham supplies the fair numbers. I put them beside the market, mark the disagreements, and decide which files deserve the next hour of work. This is the opening Week 1 sheet, with every game accounted for.

The week starts before the weekend does: Seattle on Wednesday, the Melbourne game on Thursday, eight games at once on Sunday morning, four in the afternoon, then Sunday night and Monday. The schedule is the first constraint. Clear the early deadlines, do the crowded windows in advance, and keep the late games open for later information.

Philadelphia is the largest disagreement on this copy. The Giants and Denver follow; Green Bay deserves a careful look because the two sheets name different favorites. A large gap is a reason to investigate. Nothing on this fax is an order sent downstairs.
scheduleMemo: All 16 games, all kickoff times Pacific. Eight games share Sunday’s 10:00 window and four share 13:25. Those twelve files need their first proper review before the weekend rush.
changeMemo: FORMAT CHANGE: The prior report-session sheet is filed in the archive. This begins Bill’s weekly NFL review of Graham’s Private Line; the old baseball carryovers are closed. There is no prior Bill NFL edition to manufacture a week-to-week change from.

SOURCE CHECK: This copy uses Graham’s completed September 8 information review and the Pinnacle spread observations printed with each game. Graham’s fair numbers retain their own original timestamps and provisional status. A recent review does not mean every fair number was newly made today.

MARKET TAPE: All 16 saved market deltas are zero on this source snapshot. The spread benchmarks were unchanged from the day’s retained baseline to the quoted observation. The gaps below compare Graham with Pinnacle; they are a different measurement from movement.

EDITION RHYTHM: One complete opening fax, with a second late-week edition when the personnel file, fair numbers or market materially changes. Each new edition will say what changed and what has already kicked off. Quiet files do not need a fresh speech every day.

reviews.read: Seattle opens the file at three and a half on Graham’s sheet against a three-point benchmark. Half a point is a modest disagreement, and this game has the shortest runway on the schedule. I want the final personnel picture before giving that half-point more weight. The opener gets the first check because its clock runs out first.
reviews.note: First deadline. Do the last check before the lounge fills.

reviews.read: Graham has the Rams by two; the benchmark asks three and a half. That leaves San Francisco a point and a half stronger on his sheet. His source treats Melbourne as neutral, and the recorded receiver adjustment is already in the number. Do not charge either item twice. This is the next file to settle after the opener.
reviews.note: The home designation is ink on the schedule. Graham has this one on neutral ground.

reviews.read: Chicago is the favorite on both sheets, but Graham asks only one where the benchmark asks two and a half. Carolina is the side of the disagreement. That does not make the Panthers the better team; it means the market is requiring more separation than Graham’s fair. Keep that distinction clear when the early Sunday stack arrives.
reviews.note: A favorite can be right and the asking price can still deserve a question.

reviews.read: Both numbers land on Baltimore by three and a half. This is the clean agreement file in the early window. The latest source includes a personnel review without changing the displayed fair. Unless the information or benchmark changes, this game should consume less of the desk’s time than the genuine disagreements beside it.
reviews.note: Two sheets agree. File it, then look where they do not.

reviews.read: Pittsburgh is three on Graham’s sheet and three and a half at the benchmark. Atlanta sits on the favorable side of that half-point difference. The location around three makes the comparison worth recording, but the size of the gap does not justify turning a short note into a large opinion. Recheck the actual terms before drawing an execution conclusion.
reviews.note: Circle the half. Do not inflate it.

reviews.read: Graham makes Jacksonville seven against nine and a half at the benchmark, a two-and-a-half-point disagreement toward Cleveland. His number already carries a quarterback re-entry allowance against Cleveland. I want that uncertainty revisited, not casually subtracted again. A larger cushion on paper deserves more examination precisely because the underlying file still has a question in it.
reviews.note: The uncertainty is already on Graham’s sheet. No second charge.

reviews.read: Cincinnati is three on Graham’s sheet and four on the benchmark. Tampa Bay is one point stronger in the comparison. It belongs in the early-window review, behind the larger disagreements, with special care over what price and spread are actually available together. The difference between these two numbers is the starting question, not a completed order.
reviews.note: One point of disagreement. Keep the price attached to the number.

reviews.read: Graham asks Tennessee to lay three and a half; the benchmark asks one. The two-and-a-half-point gap puts Tennessee among my first Sunday morning reviews. Both sheets choose the same favorite, so the question is the size of the advantage. Reconcile the current personnel file and check whether this much separation survives the next edition.
reviews.note: Same favorite. Different margin. This file stays on top.

reviews.read: Detroit is five on Graham’s sheet and seven at the benchmark, leaving the disagreement with New Orleans. The source already includes Detroit personnel adjustments in that five. Keep the adjusted fair intact while checking for any later information that changes those inputs. This is a two-point question within an eight-game morning window; it needs its work done before Sunday.
reviews.note: The adjustment has been made. Review the next fact, not the same fact twice.

reviews.read: Graham makes Buffalo two and a half; the benchmark has Buffalo by one. This is a point and a half toward Buffalo, with agreement on the favorite. It earns a proper review alongside Carolina and the larger early-window gaps. If the number moves, distinguish a changed market from a changed Graham opinion before rewriting the file.
reviews.note: Keep two columns: his number and their number.

reviews.read: The Chargers are eight on Graham’s sheet against ten and a half at the benchmark. Arizona is two and a half points stronger by comparison. Graham’s source already includes the Chargers’ personnel adjustment; the next task is to see whether the updated line and personnel picture still support this much disagreement. This goes near the top of the afternoon stack.
reviews.note: Eight and ten and a half are different assignments.

reviews.read: This one changes the favorite. Graham has Green Bay by one and a half while the benchmark has Minnesota by one, producing two and a half points toward Green Bay. Read both signs carefully: this is more than a half-point disagreement about the same favorite. Settle the current information file before deciding why the two sheets face different directions.
reviews.note: Check the favorite before you compare the size. Green Bay on Graham’s sheet.

reviews.read: Las Vegas is three on Graham’s sheet and three and a half at the benchmark. Miami is the side of a half-point difference. Record the position around three, then keep the desk’s attention proportionate. Philadelphia, Green Bay and Arizona have larger questions in this same kickoff window, so this file should remain concise unless something changes.
reviews.note: A small gap gets a small file until the facts enlarge it.

reviews.read: Philadelphia is eight on Graham’s sheet against four and a half at the benchmark: the week’s largest displayed disagreement, three and a half points toward Philadelphia. Graham’s source already incorporates the Washington tackle adjustment. That makes the durability of the underlying personnel assessment the first question I would revisit. The biggest gap earns the closest review, not an automatic order.
reviews.note: Largest gap on the fax. Check the support underneath it.

reviews.read: Graham gives the Giants a half-point edge; the benchmark makes Dallas the two-and-a-half-point favorite. Three points separate the sheets, and they disagree on the favorite. The source includes both a Dallas personnel adjustment and an unresolved New York personnel allowance. Sunday night provides more time to resolve those questions, not permission to treat them as resolved tonight.
reviews.note: Different favorites. Keep the personnel file open through the weekend.

reviews.read: Graham has this game at pick while the benchmark asks Kansas City to lay three. Denver is three points stronger in the comparison. Graham’s source still carries a Kansas City quarterback-clearance allowance and a Denver edge-absence adjustment. This is the last game on the fax; a Saturday note cannot stand in for Monday’s final information. Carry the questions forward explicitly.
reviews.note: Monday gets its own final check. Do not close the folder on Saturday.

closingWatchlist: FIRST DEADLINES: Finish Seattle’s personnel check before Wednesday’s opener, then revisit the San Francisco–Rams file before Thursday. The latter has a meaningful disagreement and a neutral-site treatment already built into Graham’s number.

SUNDAY MORNING: Tennessee and Cleveland lead the numerical disagreements at two and a half points; New Orleans follows at two. Carolina and Buffalo belong in the next review stack. Eight simultaneous kickoffs leave little room for discovering an unfinished file at the window.

SUNDAY AFTERNOON: Philadelphia receives the deepest review at three and a half points. Arizona and Green Bay each show two and a half. Green Bay–Minnesota requires an explicit favorite check; Graham favors Green Bay and the benchmark favors Minnesota.

LATE FILES: The Giants and Denver each show three points of disagreement. Carry the documented personnel questions forward to the proper game-day review. An early fax preserves the question; it does not answer a later fact.

NO ORDER: This is Bill’s interpretation of a dated board. None of the 16 source rows contains a proposed wager at issue time. Preserve Graham’s numbers, keep the market timestamps attached, and let the execution desk qualify any eventual order.
signature: Leave this copy on the upstairs table. Bring back the changed facts. — Bill
currentMood: Opening Week 1 private fax: all 16 Graham games reviewed in kickoff order. Philadelphia, the Giants and Denver lead the displayed disagreements; Green Bay changes the favorite. Opening-game deadlines first, crowded Sunday windows next. No order issued.
